summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, and a history of atrial tachycardia was admitted for left-sided pleuritic chest pain that began after hemodialysis. Evaluation revealed musculoskeletal chest pain, likely exacerbated by volume overload from recent dietary salt intake. Her pain was reproducible on exam and improved with analgesics. Cardiac workup, including serial troponins and EKG, showed no acute ischemia. She had mild leukocytosis from resolving inguinal boils, which improved without antibiotics. Her INR was supratherapeutic, so Coumadin was held. She underwent scheduled hemodialysis, which improved fluid status and symptoms. She remained in sinus rhythm on amiodarone, and her pain resolved sufficiently for discharge. She was discharged to extended care with instructions to monitor INR, restart Coumadin when appropriate, adhere to a low-sodium diet, and follow up with her primary care provider.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Carbuncle and furuncle of other specified sites
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
